stories.title: Ukraine's postal workers deliver lifeline under Russian fire
stories.summary: The state post service delivers pensions, medicine and letters to people just miles from the front.
stories.article_text_excerpt: Figure caption, Watch: Ukraine's post office innovation helps isolated communities By James Landale Reporting from Zaporizhzhia oblast Published 15 September 2026 Every morning Igor Smelyansky looks at a vast map of Ukraine on his office wall and decides where he should put his people in harm's way. His aides provide him with live intelligence about Russian attacks and he deploys his teams, balancing their potential operational success against risk to life or limb. But Smelyansky is no military commander. He is the head of Ukraine's state postal service, Ukrposhta. And every day he must decide how far to send his postmen and women into the deadly "kill zone" along the front lines where the threat of drone attack is ever present. "If it's too dangerous to go today, we won't go," Smelyansky told us. "We'll go tomorrow, or we'll go somewhere else. The key is to be as agile as you can." Ukrposhta does more than just collect letters and parcels. It pays out pensions in hard cash, it takes payment for utility bills.
